problem: The example treats the whole 55.6 Ah as delivered in the CC phase (5.56 h at 10 A) and then adds a 2 h taper on top. But the taper also pushes charge in: roughly (10 + 2)/2 × 2 = 12 Ah here. So the battery would receive about 55.6 + 12 ≈ 68 Ah against the 55.6 Ah needed, and a real CC phase would end earlier. A sharp student will notice the double counting.
fix: Add one line: 'This model assumes all the required Ah go in during CC; in practice the taper adds charge too (about 12 Ah here), so the CC phase would be shorter.' Or give the taper charge separately and subtract it.

problem: 'Three-hour duration is common for escape lighting' is stated as if universal. Required autonomy is set by the local code and varies; some codes ask for about one hour, others three hours. A student may quote 3 h as a rule.
fix: Write: 'The required autonomy comes from the applicable code; escape lighting is commonly specified for 1 h to 3 h, and the battery must be sized for that duration.'

problem: Two small points. The voltage curve starts at 11.5 V, which is below the open-circuit voltage of a 12 V lead-acid block at 50% depth of discharge (about 12.1 V), and well below what it reads under a 10 A charge. Also the caption says the current tapers 'while voltage rises to 14.4 V and holds', which suggests the voltage is still rising during the taper, although the plot has it flat at 14.4 V from 5.6 h.
fix: Start the voltage near 12.1 V, rising quickly to about 13 V under 10 A, and 14.4 V at 5.6 h. Reword the caption: 'current then tapers to 2 A at 7.6 h while the voltage stays at 14.4 V'.
